correctness.rationale: The wedge pairing kills quotient degree five for any nonzero relation. If minimal support is three, splitting off the complementary two-space gives ideal ranks 5 and 4 in degrees three and four. If support is at least four, a nonzero annihilator of the degree-four ideal would force both relations into v∧V and support at most three, so degree four vanishes. In support four the same annihilator argument applied inside the support gives all of Λ³U, with two extra independent dimensions from wedging the complement, hence cubic quotient dimension four. For support five some pencil member α has rank four, since two independent decomposable members have joint support at most four. Write the other generator as β+e∧x relative to the support U of α. The invertible wedge map α∧−:U→Λ³U eliminates the pure-U component, leaving image contributions from x∧U+kα+kβ in the component e∧Λ²U. The rank of that span drops from five to four exactly when a pencil member with nonzero e-component is decomposable; two such points cannot occur. This uses alternating rank and perfect pairings even in characteristic two, not division by 2 or a wedge-square test. Unique minimal support gives C3 and C4. For C5,1 the fixed decomposable point count is Möbius inversion on V/S(ω) with coefficients 1,−1,q and zero contribution from dimension zero; the per-point factor simplifies to q⁴(q+1)(q³−1). Independent Gaussian polynomial expansion gives C5,0/C5,1=q(q−1) and proves positivity together with e12,e34 as a support-four witness. Independent replay (python /workspace/branches/independent-reproductions/algebra_reproduction.py) computes actual wedge ranks for all 174251 binary two-subspaces and gives 1085,16926,52080,104160 in the claimed order. The binary experiment does not prove the uniform theorem; the displayed rank and counting arguments do. Frozen verify.py was inspected, not executed.

evidence: A relation two-space is a projective line in P(Λ²V); decomposable members are precisely its Fq-points on Gr(2,V). Exterior quotient dimensions depend also on the common contraction support, not just on how many decomposable points are on the line.

For example, over F2 the line spanned by e12+e34 and e12+e13+e24 has no decomposable point but support four (each of its three Pfaffians on that support is 1), unlike the full-support external-line stratum.
The inspected generic exterior-algebra prior uses skew-symmetric pencil normal forms over algebraically closed characteristic not two.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Binary external-line statistics cannot be equated solely with the support-five zero-decomposable stratum. A pencil normal form over an algebraic closure does not by itself count rational lines or finite-field membership of the rank-drop locus. The independently reconstructed wedge step is needed to turn rank/drop data into all four Hilbert profiles.

value.rationale: The Hilbert series is a natural invariant of exterior ideals, and the first five-generator case exposes two distinct full-support behaviours which the generic series and binary line census alone do not explain uniformly. The complete distribution relates cubic syzygies to rank-two incidence, works in characteristic two, and gives exact proportions for arbitrary finite fields. It is not an orbit or Betti-table classification, and the worth of the result does not depend on treating the generic row or the q=2 recomputation as novel.
